svg.text: Concept: ball-lens bead + yellow filter over the phone camera, lit by the phone's own flash, for Nile-Red-stained microplastics on a glass slide

g.text: Ø1–3 mm spherical bead in jig
The flash, through a blue gel, lights the membrane at an angle via the acrylic guide.
Stained plastics fluoresce, the bead magnifies them, and the yellow filter passes only
the orange-red emission to the camera, so no extra battery or LED is needed.
f = focus gap, set by jig height ≈ working distance of the bead
self-aligns the bead to the lens

svg.text: Stained plastics glow orange-red on a dark field

g.text: blocks blue light, passes the glow
Nile Red binds to plastic surfaces and fluoresces orange-red (~580–650 nm) under blue–green light (~450–550 nm).
The yellow long-pass filter blocks the excitation light, so only stained particles glow on a dark field.
Caveat: natural organic matter also takes up the stain, so pre-digest with H₂O₂ or filter by size/shape in the app.
